title: AI agents help with security design reviews and threat modelling
problem: Security design reviews are a chronic bottleneck because specialists gather context by hand while developers wait.
approach: Anthropic's application security team says Claude assists threat modelling; Cloudflare runs a spec reviewer agent over design specifications before implementation.
Stripe is scheduled to describe agents running the review lifecycle (talk not yet given); human experts take complex architectural decisions.
Stripe reports reviews going from weeks to minutes; Cloudflare reviewed close to 600 specs since May 2026 (both self-reported).

title: Security guardrails for AI-written code, with oversight set by code criticality
problem: Coding agents write production code that people review less, and studies find security flaws in a large share of AI-generated code.
approach: Security checks sit in the coding agent's loop: scans of every touched file, package firewalls, and security instruction files and rule packs.
Developers review and test AI output as for any code; the UK NCSC advises manual coding for authentication, secrets and safety-critical code.
Over 3 million write-time scans a week, 95% under 5 seconds (vendor-published); AI-generated code passes security 56% on average (vendor-published).

title: Disclosure and human accountability rules for AI-assisted code contributions
problem: Tool-generated contributions raise submission volume while reviewer and maintainer bandwidth is scarce, and provenance and legal certification of AI-written code are unclear.
approach: The Linux kernel project bars AI agents from adding Signed-off-by tags, because only humans can certify the contributor's legal statement.
It asks for an Assisted-by tag naming the model, and a reproducer and tested fix for any bug an assistant finds.
A human certifies origin and reviews the code before submission; no measured outcome is published.

title: AI review of every pull request, including a dedicated security reviewer agent
problem: Merge requests queue for hours awaiting first review, and single-prompt AI review produced vague suggestions and noise, while lightweight security checks miss context-dependent vulnerabilities.
approach: Cloudflare runs up to seven specialised reviewer agents per merge request; a coordinator removes duplicates, rates severity and can block serious problems.
Engineers can override a block: 288 times, 0.6% of merge requests; 131,246 review runs in the first 30 days (self-reported).
At Atlassian a security review agent had 54% of comments validated by security engineers in a shadow deployment (self-reported).

title: Engineering standards rewritten as machine-readable rules that review agents enforce
problem: Standards live in documents, chat threads and individual memory, so no engineer can read every standard and reviewers cannot reliably check every requirement.
approach: Cloudflare rebuilt its standards as a governed 'Codex'; an agent extracts rules that review agents retrieve for code, specifications and incident reports.
Domain owners approve and promote documents; only those promoted to 'enforced' block merges, and engineers act on findings.
Close to 230,000 standards violations flagged, almost 16,000 withheld approval (self-reported).

title: Risk-tiered automated review that lands low-risk code changes without a human reviewer
problem: AI coding agents increase code volume faster than reviewers can read it, and at Meta the share of changes getting timely review fell.
approach: Meta's RADAR scores each change for risk, runs AI code review and deterministic validation, and lands qualifying changes without a human reviewer.
Changes failing the eligibility, risk-score or validation gates stay on the normal human review path.
Meta reports 331K+ changes landed, a revert rate one third and production incident rate one fiftieth of non-RADAR diffs (self-reported).

title: Scanning every code change before submission, with an agent proving reachability
problem: One-off scans of large code bases are slow and short on context, so vulnerabilities are found late while AI increases the amount of code needing security.
approach: Google's AI Infrastructure team scans each check-in with agents; a triage agent tests whether the vulnerable path is reachable.
A bug-fix agent drafts fixes that go to human review in the change request; no checkpoint is stated for triage verdicts.
Triage agent over 92% precision in under a minute; hundreds of vulnerabilities stopped per month (self-reported).

title: AI reasoning-based code scanning used alongside rule-based static analysis
problem: Rule-based scanners find only what someone wrote a rule for, miss business-logic and access-control flaws, and create noise that teams spend time triaging.
approach: Agentic scanners from OpenAI, Anthropic, Wiz, Semgrep and Snyk build an editable threat model, test findings in a sandbox and propose fixes.
An analyst or developer reviews validated findings and approves patches; nothing is applied without human approval.
OpenAI's beta cut noise 84% in one case and over-reported severity over 90% (vendor-published); GitHub's researcher reported 24 Android vulnerabilities (self-reported).
who: OpenAI, Anthropic, Wiz, Semgrep, Snyk, GitHub

title: Reachability-first triage and closure tracking for AI-generated vulnerability candidates
problem: AI-assisted programmes generate more vulnerability candidates and patch pull requests than teams can review, so an opened pull request is not a fixed bug.
approach: Rubrik's product security lead is scheduled to describe (talk not yet given) a loop taking findings to merge, rejection, deferral or acceptance.
It uses root-cause de-duplication, reachability ranking and no auto-patching of bug classes that cannot be validated cheaply; engineers review before merge.
No operating-loop results are published.

title: Validator-gated AI testing of an organisation's own running web applications
problem: AI code scanners flood security teams with unverified hypotheses, so a real flaw is hard to tell from a convincing hallucination, and candidates come without proof of exploitability.
approach: Google's PageBreak agent hypothesises web flaws in Google's own applications; a validator not written by AI confirms each against a running environment.
Only deterministically validated findings go to product teams; unconfirmed ones are kept as seeds for later scans.
PageBreak found over 500 cross-site scripting flaws in Google's first-party applications since a 2025 pilot (self-reported).

title: AI agents build custom analysis tools and formal models before manual audits
problem: Reviewing code in a new virtual machine with a custom assembly language and almost no tooling is slow, and manual review alone may miss classes of bugs.
approach: Before auditing the Miden virtual machine, Trail of Bits spent six months having agents build a language server, decompiler and formal model.
Auditors use and check the tools during manual review; the audit had 95 machine-checked proofs and one high-severity issue (self-reported).

title: AI-drafted fixes for scanner alerts and critical vulnerabilities, delivered as reviewable changes
problem: Developers often have little secure-coding training, so fixing scanner alerts takes substantial effort, and finding vulnerabilities is only half the work.
approach: LLMs draft a fix for an alert or vulnerability as a proposed change: GitHub's Copilot Autofix, Google's bug-fix agent, Meta's AI-written diffs.
A developer reviews and accepts or edits every suggested fix.
Meta is scheduled to report (talk not yet given) over 40% of critical vulnerabilities fixed by AI-written diffs (self-reported).

title: AI agent applies compiler bounds-safety annotations to remove whole classes of bugs
problem: Patching one bug at a time does not remove whole classes of memory-safety vulnerability, such as the libwebp heap overflow used in a zero-click iPhone exploit.
approach: DeepMind's CodeMender agent applied compiler bounds-safety annotations to parts of libwebp, fixing its own compile errors and test failures.
Patches reach human reviewers only after static and dynamic analysis, differential testing, fuzzing and solver checks.
It upstreamed 72 security fixes during the research (self-reported); this is a pilot.

title: Automated AI screening of inbound packages, agent skills and outside pull requests
problem: Malicious packages reach developer machines before pull-request scans, models invent package names, skill marketplaces carry malicious skills, and anonymous pull requests can reach CI secrets.
approach: Automated gates screen inbound code: Semgrep's AI-assisted malware rules, Snyk's package firewall, ClawHub and Cisco skill scanners, OpenSearch's model gate.
An expert verifies Semgrep's malware rules before publishing; no human check is stated for OpenSearch's gate.
Independent testing bypassed all deployed skill scanners tested with four purpose-built malicious skills (independent).

title: AI-assisted research for curators of a vulnerability advisory database
problem: Advisory submissions surged, and the hard ones need package disambiguation, version-range reconstruction and reconciling conflicting upstream data, all of which takes human time.
approach: GitHub gave curators AI assistance in the research phase of advisory review, and better automation for extracting upstream CVE data.
Curators make every decision, and reviewed advisories remain human-validated.
1,560 advisories were reviewed in May 2026, over five times a typical month (self-reported).

title: Testing AI security tools on contamination-reduced, audited benchmarks before trusting them
problem: Public benchmarks built from known CVEs can be memorised by models, exploit-only checks inflate results, and one scan can miss a bug the next run finds.
approach: Teams build their own harnesses: GitLab measures false positives and misses, AWS audits every success on refreshed CVE benchmarks, Semgrep tests memorisation.
Experts review graders' verdicts, as Trail of Bits does.
Semgrep found 93 of 176 judged solutions near-identical to real code (vendor-published); exploit-only validation inflated patching results 1.83 times (independent).
who: GitLab, AWS, Semgrep, Trail of Bits

title: Security team rebuilt around building and operating its own AI skills
problem: Trail of Bits says most companies hand out chat licences without changing workflows; a year earlier about 95% of its staff were sceptical or resistant.
approach: Trail of Bits standardised on one coding agent, wrote an AI handbook of approved tools, and built a curated skills marketplace.
Anthropic's application security engineers each own a Claude-powered security system; humans remain the auditors, under handbook approval rules.
Trail of Bits reports 94 plugins, 201 skills and 84 agents, and 200 bugs a week on the right engagements (self-reported).
who: Trail of Bits, Anthropic, GitLab, Cloudflare
